subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.
reasoning:
I'm planning the hydra's design in a God of War style: a low, bulky quadruped body with stubby legs, a tail, and five long necks fanning out with heads, all rendered dark and battle-worn with scars, runic markings, ember-glowing eyes, bone armor plates, and chains.

Now I'm sketching out the actual skeleton structure — hips as root, a spine chain building up the body, limb chains for the legs, a tail chain, and five separate neck chains branching from the chest using curved catmull paths that rise and fan outward, each ending in a skull with jaw joints, teeth, horns, and glowing eyes. I'm working out the scale (roughly 3m body, 3.5m tall with necks raised) and defining the joint coordinates and chain parameters for the spine and tail sweeps.

Still working out leg placement and limb chains...

Still computing neck curve points...

Defining the head joint next, attaching it to the last neck joint with a forward-down direction, then planning to build the head geometry as a lofted frustum box oriented along that direction.

Now I'm sketching the skull, snout, and jaw as a sequence of frustum boxes along the head bone's local axes—narrowing shapes for the skull, a thinner snout, and a separate jaw joint aimed downward for the lower mandible—then adding spikes along the jaw edges to represent teeth.

For the open-mouth pose, I'm considering rotating the jaw bone about the world x-axis by a small positive angle, but I realize the head's local "forward" direction is tied to the model's own axes rather than the head's actual pointing direction, so there's a slight mismatch I'll just accept rather than trying to perfectly correct for head tilt.

I decide instead to fix the head's forward direction to be mostly horizontal with just a slight x-offset, letting the neck curve down into it, which simplifies the jaw math. For the eyes, I'm placing glowing orange spheres positioned relative to the head bone, then thinking through how to add a slit pupil -- maybe a textured plane with an SVG eye graphic facing outward rather than a plain dark shape.

I settle on a simpler approach: glow sphere plus a small flattened black ellipsoid parented in front for the pupil. Then I plan the horns as swept bezier spikes from the skull, a brow ridge box, tiny dark nostrils, and mane spikes running along the neck using an "along" helper to place several spike shapes at intervals.

For the neck sweep, I need to construct a Sweep object first before passing it to the along helper. Then I think through body detailing—rune-glowing scars as glowing decals on the flank, and iron collar/shackle bands with chain links around the necks, though the shackle attachment point feels a bit risky to pull off cleanly.

Instead of risking a failed loop cut, I switch to building the cuff as a torus geometry positioned and oriented along the neck's tangent, with radius interpolated along the neck's taper. I settle on placing a cuff plus a spike stud on a couple of the necks to suggest broken chain tails.

Then I plan a ring of small spikes jutting outward around a chain point as if bone studs, dorsal spikes swept along the body's top line for back plates, and consider but skip a cauterized hydra stump. For the belly I'm starting to set up a countershaded scale pattern for the underside coloring.

For textures I'm settling on two: a glowing rune decal and a lava-cracked scar texture, with jagged orange crack lines for the scar glow, plus a rune decal applied along the body flanks for an emblem-like effect.

Now I'm positioning the decal on the body surface near the belly, verifying the projection direction and size work against the surface curvature, then moving to the feet: aligning sole box heights so the bottom sits flush at ground level, matching leg tube radius at the ankle join.

Then I'm adding the foot box and forward-pointing claw spikes parented to the leg tip joint, before setting up a swept chain for the leg with a tapering thigh radius function.

I'm checking height placement so nothing clips below ground, confirming the belly and tail tip stay above zero, then moving into color metadata—skin, bone, iron, ember, mouth, and teeth tones—and refining head details like the inner mouth, a small tongue, and a neck-colored head paint layer.

Now I'm setting up per-head variation, scaling one center head slightly bigger than the rest, and writing the function that builds each head's skull geometry using tapered boxes sized relative to the neck joint.

Still writing head geometry... now adding snout, lower jaw bone with its own joint and taper, and starting to place teeth along the jaw as small positioned shapes.

Confirming jaw pose happens after teeth are built so positions stay correct, then sketching the horn sweeps with bezier curves anchored at head-local points, and starting on a brow box positioned over the eyes.

Still working out neck curve coordinates...

Still defining leg joint chains...

I'm adding hip muscle spheres, designing a rune texture SVG with interlocked valknut triangles, a jagged lava-crack scar texture, importing the glow kit, and setting up spikes swept along the body using bone-colored cones.

I'm now adding shoulder armor: iron pauldron plates as half-sphere geometries positioned and rotated at the shoulders, keeping colors simple with plain paint instead of a metal shader kit.
